fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The autodidact who outgrew the classroom", "body": "James Frosch tells Chance Garton he was homeschooled in southern Louisiana until eighth grade and had no internet at home until he was fourteen or fifteen, so he learned in libraries, in museums and from source documents. Entering public school felt like a ceiling dropping over what he was allowed to study, because anything that would not be on the test was dismissed as not worth knowing. He started nursing, switched to micro molecular biology, then left college once he decided how much we actually know is very flimsy. Curiosity driven investigation, he argues, is the opposite of forced memorization."}, {"title": "Your health is true wealth", "body": "Frosch sells fresh edible and medicinal mushrooms at a Louisiana farmers market under a motto printed on his tent, your health is true wealth. He explains that edible mushrooms carry beta glucans, complex carbohydrates that feed the probiotic microbiome, aid detoxification and engage the lymphatic system, and that the microbiome is spread through the tissues rather than confined to the gut. He urges people to eat what grows in their own area, because a wild mushroom breathes the same air, drinks the same water and moves under the same cycles of sun and moon that you do."}, {"title": "The Christed mind and the Luciferic mind", "body": "Working from an esoteric frame, Frosch describes a Luciferic mind that seeks to know and a Christed mind that accepts how things were made. He calls the intellectual mind a usurper that defines everything through number, symbol and pattern, and says it must be taken off the throne so the heart can be crowned again. Garton widens it, tracing Lucifer back to Venus and to lux fero, light carrier, and reading Christ, Hermes and Odin as one symbol for the eye behind all eyes. Both land on the same verdict, a great servant and a poor master."}, {"title": "Fungi as the cleanup crew", "body": "Garton raises the doctrine of signatures, the idea that a plant's form hints at what it heals, and Frosch answers that mycelial networks mirror the nervous system and grow radially symmetrical, flowing around obstacles like slow water. He walks through basidiomycetes, ascomycetes and dimorphic fungi such as candida, and describes spores as resistant eggs that could sit in the sands of the Sahara waiting for the right stimulus. Fungi break down glyphosate and even plastic, which is why he warns against eating mushrooms picked from a sprayed lawn, since the toxin is still held in the body."}, {"title": "The trip that turned into a livelihood", "body": "Frosch says a potent psilocybin experience told him to do the work he now does, and that watching his mother climb to roughly fifteen prescriptions a day with no relief pushed him toward providing medicine instead. Family Fungi grows, dehydrates, powders, encapsulates and tinctures everything on site, offering a five mushroom extract of chaga, reishi, lion's mane, turkey tail and shiitake along with grow kits. He cites Terence McKenna on societies trading mushroom initiations for alcohol, and tells Garton that buying from him means entering a relationship rather than a transaction."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: James is the inspored intellect behind Family Fungi, a holistic wellness homestead providing mushroom based medicines and do-it-yourself wisdom. We discuss his self-directed education, aligning with your environment, seeing the Logos pattern, enzymes and your endocrine system, and more.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: The Plus+ Extension forages into coffee, chaga, and adaptagens, the difference between mycellium and the mushroom fruit body, maintaining our lymphatic system, our ecology of health practices, and tales of turkey tail.
